project.name: ci-diagnosis-mcp
project.objective: Build a Python MCP server (mcp SDK 2.x, stdio) that diagnoses failed GitHub Actions runs for coding agents: it collects log and metadata evidence, keeps a mode and origin belief, ranks the next evidence to gather, and returns structured, agent-native diagnoses as specified in DESIGN.md v2.

decisions.title: Language and SDK: Python with mcp 2.x
decisions.text: Server is Python using the official mcp SDK 2.x (MCPServer, formerly FastMCP) over stdio. Chosen because the maintainer reads Python, not TypeScript; the SDK is official and installable with uvx/pip. TypeScript scaffold from the first attempt was discarded.

decisions.title: Belief is two variables: mode and origin
decisions.text: A single root-cause label mixed what failed with why. Mode (what the log shows) is set by parsers with decisive weights; origin (this_change, pre_existing, flaky, environment, external) is a Bayesian posterior fed by diff, history, matrix, attempts and rerun channels. Adopted after an independent design review found overlapping hypotheses, under-confidence on easy cases, and double counting in the single-variable design.

decisions.title: No model call inside the server
decisions.text: The server does deterministic extraction and Bayesian updating only; the calling agent is the reasoner. Avoids a second model's cost, latency, API key, and non-determinism, and keeps the engine unit-testable.

decisions.title: GitHub Actions first, stdio only, no rerun side effect in v1
decisions.text: First provider is GitHub Actions; analysis layer stays provider-agnostic. Transport is stdio (local agents). rerun_job is excluded from v1 because it needs actions:write and agents already have gh run rerun; rerun results still enter as evidence via attempt linking.

decisions.title: Within-channel combination and tempering
decisions.text: Per channel: max of supporting weights times min of opposing weights per origin; channels multiply; tempering T from {0.5,0.7,1.0} chosen on the fixture corpus, default 0.7; no per-channel cap (nothing sums). Fixes the review finding that max-only silently discarded opposing evidence and that the cap was unreachable.

decisions.title: Process: Genesis with minimal human gates and model reviewers
decisions.text: Owner wants automation and a 2-3 hour build. Human approvals are limited to the two Genesis-mandated gates (spec, plan), each given once. Tasks are classified honestly; model reviews (Opus 5.5 for design, Sonnet 5.5 for code) are run in fresh contexts and recorded as decisions with reasons, not as blocking gates, except where Genesis auto-adds independent-review for medium risk, which the owner approves in one batch. Approver name: Shrikant Pawade. Builder: Fable 5.1 in this session; no ultracode fan-out because the parts are sequentially dependent.

decisions.title: Spec review (Opus 5.5): APPROVE_WITH_CHANGES; disposition of each item
decisions.text: Reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh context, read-only, given SPEC.md and DESIGN.md. Verdict APPROVE_WITH_CHANGES. Builder disposition: MUST_FIX 1 accepted: whole-log check always runs on pre-filtered lines; slice{window,mismatch} exposed; AC-3 asserts exact values; DESIGN s13/s19 aligned. MUST_FIX 2 accepted: attempts observations defined relative to the attempt under investigation with weights; run_attempt input added. MUST_FIX 3 accepted: availability rule with unavailable_actions[], observed means at least one observation, equivalence stop requires mode confidence not low and overrides the two-channel rule. MUST_FIX 4 accepted: required output keys bound in FR-17 and asserted by AC-6. MUST_FIX 5 accepted: ordered derivation rules, test-path globs, null label, mixed case in AC-8. MUST_FIX 6 accepted: excerpts fenced with longer backtick runs and labelled untrusted; lines capped at 2000 chars before matching; new AC-13. MUST_FIX 7 accepted: umask 077, dir 0700, repo regex, cache files by job id; new AC-14. MUST_FIX 8 accepted: Authorization only to the API host; AC-12 scans content, errors, stderr and cache; unprovable clause dropped. MUST_FIX 9 accepted: fixtures and expected.json committed before parser code as a separate task with a ledger trace; three adversarial unknown cases; unknown-rate definition fixed. MUST_FIX 10 accepted as cut: AC-4 replay moved out of v0.1; ranking formula unit-tested instead. MUST_FIX 11 accepted: mcp>=2,<3; NFR-7 says direct dependencies. SHOULD_FIX 1-9 all accepted (failed conclusions, startup_failure, repo-relative paths, 20 MB log_text cap, 410/in-progress/scope errors, cheap ACs for stdout purity, determinism, candidate_runs, token order, AC-7 content density, AC-11 redirect counting, smoothing pseudo-count 1, progress notifications, mode runner-up and step_context kept). CUT_IF_LATE applied now to protect the 2-3 hour budget: cut 1 (AC-4), cut 2 (add_evidence/retract_evidence removed from v0.1; agent can reason without them), cut 3 (level-2 extra-log downloads removed; level-1 signatures only), cut 4 (per-repo prior updates removed; outcomes stored, global prior used), cut 5 partially (gradle/maven, docker, cargo deferred; formatters kept because their regexes are trivial), cut 6 (rebuild-from-GitHub and AC-9 replaced by a not-found error), cut 7 (over-20 MB logs use a plain tail cap of 20000 lines). Reason for accepting cuts: reviewer and builder agree the parser list and GitHub-backed actions would not fit the budget; every cut is additive later and none touches FR-4 or the generic fallback, which guard the top risk.

decisions.title: Plan review (Sonnet 5.5): APPROVE_WITH_CHANGES; disposition
decisions.text: Reviewer: Claude Sonnet 5.5, fresh context, read-only, given PLAN.md, SPEC.md and DESIGN.md s8/10/11/13/16. Disposition: MUST_FIX 1 accepted: T1 ships no parser (generic fallback moved to the start of T2b); git repo and baseline commit exist (d5f60a5); a test asserts the first commit touching tests/fixtures precedes the first touching analysis/parsers. MUST_FIX 2 accepted: T1 proves slicing mechanics (window values) on inline logs; AC-3's fixture assertions are delivered by test_corpus in T2b; T7's full-suite gate binds it; task requirement lists are not re-plumbed because the plan is approved and a reopen would cost a human approval the owner declined. MUST_FIX 3 accepted: analysis/pipeline.py in T2b. MUST_FIX 4 partly moot: pyproject and venv already exist; a dependency-set test is added to T4; __main__.py and the scripts entry go in T6. MUST_FIX 5 rejected as a plan change for the same reason as item 2; T5 is instead implemented as three modules (resolve/download, cluster/channels, gather/outcome) with tests per module; the token-order half of AC-16 is tested under T4's gate. MUST_FIX 6 accepted: tests/test_perf.py for NFR-2/3; AC-12 tool-output half in T6; tests/test_mode.py in T2b; fence and files tests inside test_normalize.py so T1's gate runs them; NFR-10 discovery test in T2b. MUST_FIX 7 accepted: T6 forwards progress to ctx.report_progress with an assertion. SHOULD_FIX: scopes skipped (plan change); fixture-tree hash committed in T2a and asserted by test_corpus so corpus failures cannot be fixed by editing fixtures; AC-7 timing test added to T2b's suite; test_fixes.py asserts every (mode, origin) cell; public failed run for the smoke test chosen during T4.

decisions.title: T4 code review (Sonnet 5.5): APPROVE_WITH_CHANGES; disposition
decisions.text: Reviewer: Claude Sonnet 5.5, fresh context, read-only, reproduced findings with httpx.MockTransport. Accepted and fixed in the T4 follow-up commit: (1 high) paginate followed off-host Link next URLs with the token: now only same-scheme-and-host next links are followed; (2 high) env tokens not stripped and transport errors leaked raw messages: tokens stripped, every httpx error wrapped into GitHubError with a fixed message; (3) 3xx on API calls now raise GitHubError (moved); (4) 429 and retry-after 403 are rate limits, annotations() swallows only 404 and scope 403; (5) log size cap keeps the tail and prepends a visible truncation notice; (6) 308 added, Location joined with urljoin, cap applied to the non-redirect path; (7) validate_repo uses fullmatch so trailing newlines are rejected; (8) State.__init__ sets umask and chmods the directory and logs dir, cache files are created with os.open 0600; (9) cache uses bytes UTF-8 so carriage returns survive; (10) purge tolerates concurrent deletion; (11) gh auth token takes --hostname from GITHUB_API_URL. (12) scope note accepted: the NFR-1 parser-gate changes rode in the T4 commit because the perf fix was found during T4; recorded here rather than rewriting history. Test gaps 1-5 addressed with new tests in test_github_client.py and test_state.py.

decisions.title: Smoke-test findings: matrix evidence scoped to job family; logs analysed one at a time
decisions.text: Live run pallets/flask#37633292268 showed two defects. (1) A lone 'typing' job failing beside twelve unrelated green jobs produced '1 of 13 matrix jobs failed' evidence (environment strong), which is wrong: matrix evidence now counts only jobs sharing the failed job's name prefix, so heterogeneous job sets add no matrix evidence. (2) mypy --pretty wraps messages onto indented continuation lines; the mypy parser now joins up to three continuation lines and takes the [code] from the last one. Separately, NFR-3 measurement showed download() held all logs in memory; it now streams each log into the disk cache and start() analyses one log at a time (peak RSS 432 MB for 8x20 MB in a fresh process, 499 MB when contaminated by earlier tests, hence the perf test runs in a subprocess).

decisions.title: T5/T6 code review (Sonnet 5.5): APPROVE_WITH_CHANGES; disposition
decisions.text: Reviewer: Claude Sonnet 5.5, fresh context, read-only, reproduced 8 of 15 findings with scratch scripts. Accepted and fixed: (1 high) branch target now filters runs to the newest head SHA; (2) fork PRs: has_pr depends on a resolved PR number (from the pr_number target or run.pull_requests), base ref is fetched when needed; (3) truncated, errors_omitted, tests_omitted, files_omitted, root_cause_hint and level1_signature exposed on JobView and rendered, computed from pre-cap totals; (4) error results no longer carry structured_content that violates the output schema; candidate runs are listed in the text; (5) an attempt counts as passed when no job failed, timed out or was cancelled, in-progress attempts are skipped, the three nearest attempts are compared; (6) pr_history only considers runs created before the investigated run and records only signature-checked pushes; (7) base_history filters to push runs older than the investigated run and counts only level-1 signature matches among the latest three failed base runs; (8) downloads use return_exceptions, failed logs are listed in jobs_not_downloaded with the reason, an error is raised only when every download fails; (9) fetch_full_step_log without clusters asks for job_id; (10) max_jobs clamped to 15 to keep NFR-4; (11) log-derived strings outside the fence are sanitised (no backticks or newlines) and sections are labelled as from the log; (12) httpx logger set to WARNING so signed blob URLs are not logged; (13) ValueError/KeyError return a generic actionable message and log the detail; (14) fetch_sibling_jobs is marked taken only when the run has more than one job; (15) mode unknown with no actions left now returns stop. Rejected: deleting mark_channel('annotations'), because the trail should record that annotations were fetched even though they carry no origin weight. Test gaps 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 addressed with new tests; gap 4 (AC-11 counts the fake's calls rather than respx) accepted as a known limitation because the fake mirrors the client's accounting and is exercised by the respx-backed server test.

knowledge.title: mcp SDK 2.x API facts
knowledge.text: mcp 2.3.0: FastMCP renamed to MCPServer (from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer). @server.tool() auto-detects structured output from the return annotation. A tool may return mcp.types.CallToolResult directly with custom content plus structured_content; the SDK validates structured_content against the output model derived from the return annotation. run(transport='stdio'). Local venv resolved to Python 3.10, the declared minimum.
